457	          if [ "${{ needs.release-policy.outputs.lane }}" = "rc" ]; then
458	            prerelease=(--prerelease)
459	          fi
460	          if gh release view "$tag" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
461	            gh release edit "$tag" --title "$tag" --notes-file "$notes" "${prerelease[@]}"
462	            gh release upload "$tag" "${files[@]}" --clobber
463	          else
464	            gh release create "$tag" --title "$tag" --notes-file "$notes" "${prerelease[@]}" "${files[@]}"
465	          fi
466	
467	  publish-homebrew-formula:
468	    name: publish Homebrew formula
469	    if: needs.release-policy.outputs.publish_homebrew == 'true'
470	    needs:
471	      - release-policy
472	      - publish-github-release
473	    runs-on: ubuntu-22.04
474	    env:
475	      HOMEBREW_TAP_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.HOMEBREW_TAP_TOKEN }}
476	    steps:
477	      - name: Check Homebrew tap token
478	        shell: bash
479	        run: |
480	          if [[ -z "${HOMEBREW_TAP_TOKEN:-}" ]]; then
481	            echo "::error::HOMEBREW_TAP_TOKEN is required to publish gdc/homebrew-tap formulae"
482	            exit 1
483	          fi
484	      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
485	        with:
486	          repository: gdc/homebrew-tap
487	          token: ${{ secrets.HOMEBREW_TAP_TOKEN }}
488	          path: homebrew-tap
489	      - name: Download release trust bundle
490	        uses: actions/download-artifact@v4
491	        with:
492	          name: dist-trust
493	          path: target/distrib
494	      - name: Commit formula
495	        shell: bash
496	        run: |
497	          mkdir -p homebrew-tap/Formula
498	          cp target/distrib/*.rb homebrew-tap/Formula/
499	          cd homebrew-tap
500	          git config user.name "deadreckon release bot"
501	          git config user.email "release-bot@users.noreply.github.com"
502	          if git diff --quiet -- Formula; then
503	            echo "No Homebrew formula changes to publish"
504	            exit 0
505	          fi
506	          git add Formula/*.rb
507	          git commit -m "deadreckon ${GITHUB_REF_NAME#v}"
508	          git push
509	
510	  publish-npm:
511	    name: publish npm packages
512	    if: needs.release-policy.outputs.publish_npm == 'true'
513	    needs:

515	      - publish-github-release
516	    permissions:

518	      id-token: write
519	    uses: ./.github/workflows/publish-npm.yml
520	    with:

444	trait Taxonomy {
445	    fn is_retryable(&self) -> bool;
446	    fn is_fatal(&self) -> bool;
447	}
448	
449	impl Taxonomy for DeadreckonError {
450	    fn is_retryable(&self) -> bool {
451	        DeadreckonError::is_retryable(self)
452	    }
453	
454	    fn is_fatal(&self) -> bool {
455	        DeadreckonError::is_fatal(self)
456	    }
457	}
458	
459	impl Taxonomy for ProviderError {
460	    fn is_retryable(&self) -> bool {
461	        ProviderError::is_retryable(self)
462	    }
463	
464	    fn is_fatal(&self) -> bool {
465	        ProviderError::is_fatal(self)
466	    }
467	}
468	
469	impl Taxonomy for SandboxError {
470	    fn is_retryable(&self) -> bool {
471	        SandboxError::is_retryable(self)
472	    }
473	
474	    fn is_fatal(&self) -> bool {
475	        SandboxError::is_fatal(self)
476	    }
477	}
478	
479	fn assert_taxonomy<T: Taxonomy>(errors: Vec<T>) {
480	    for error in errors {
481	        assert!(
482	            error.is_retryable() || error.is_fatal(),
483	            "error variant must be retryable or fatal"
484	        );
485	        assert!(
486	            !(error.is_retryable() && error.is_fatal()),
487	            "error variant cannot be both retryable and fatal"
488	        );
489	    }
490	}

602	fn registry_kind(line: &str) -> Option<RegistryKind> {
603	    let line = line.trim();
604	    if line.starts_with("mod tests") {
605	        None
606	    } else if line.starts_with("pub use ") {
607	        Some(RegistryKind::PubUse)
608	    } else if line.starts_with("pub mod ") {

623	fn collect_pub_use_statements(text: &str) -> Vec<String> {
624	    let mut statements = Vec::new();
625	    let mut current = Vec::new();
626	    let mut in_statement = false;
627	    for line in text.lines() {
628	        let trimmed = line.trim();
629	        if !in_statement && trimmed.starts_with("pub use ") {
630	            current.push(trimmed.to_string());
631	            in_statement = true;
632	        } else if in_statement {
633	            current.push(trimmed.to_string());
634	        }
635	        if in_statement && trimmed.ends_with(';') {
636	            statements.push(current.join(" "));
637	            current.clear();
638	            in_statement = false;
639	        }
640	    }
641	    statements
642	}

659	fn identifier_tokens(text: &str) -> Vec<String> {
660	    let mut tokens = Vec::new();
661	    let mut current = String::new();
662	    for ch in text.chars() {
663	        if ch == '_' || ch.is_ascii_alphanumeric() {
664	            current.push(ch);
665	        } else if !current.is_empty() {
666	            tokens.push(std::mem::take(&mut current));
667	        }
668	    }
669	    if !current.is_empty() {
670	        tokens.push(current);
671	    }
672	    tokens.sort();
673	    tokens
674	}

I've read all three changed files in full. Let me analyze the changes through the security lens.

**ci.yml (new):**
- Triggers on `push` (all branches) and `pull_request` — NOT `pull_request_target`. This is the safe trigger choice: forks run with read-only GITHUB_TOKEN and no access to secrets.
- `permissions: contents: read` — minimal.
- `persist-credentials: false` on checkout.
- Installs `expect` (Tcl tool) from stock Ubuntu repos.
- No secrets are referenced, no write perms granted.
- CI/CD TRUST gate does not apply: requires `workflow_dispatch`/`repository_dispatch`/`pull_request_target` + secrets/write — none present.

**release.yml:**
- Only diff: `cargo test --workspace --locked` → `cargo test --workspace --locked --no-fail-fast`. Behavior change is "run all tests even if one fails before reporting failure." Still aborts the job on test failure (exit code is non-zero if any test failed). No security impact — release gating remains intact.

**tests/hygiene_config.rs:**
- `format_commit_touches_only_whitespace_and_imports` adds an early return when `git rev-parse --is-shallow-repository` returns `true`. This is a hygiene/archaeology check, not a security gate. Skipping it on shallow clones cannot enable any attacker action — it does not gate releases or sign artifacts.
- `release_binary_size_within_baseline_slack` switches to per-OS baseline (`tests/.size-baseline-{os}`) and skips when the file is missing. Binary size is a perf hygiene metric, not a security control. The path is built from `std::env::consts::OS` (compile-time constant: `linux`/`macos`/`windows`), so no path-injection surface.
- No new sinks (no shell exec of attacker data, no SQL, no FS write of attacker content, no network, no auth decision).

Neither workflow file change widens the trust boundary, exposes secrets, weakens permissions, or introduces a sink that takes attacker-controlled input. The test changes only relax purely hygienic assertions in unrelated scenarios (shallow clone, OS without pinned baseline) — neither is consulted by release-trust gating, signing, or publishing logic.
